title: Require a reproducible phonemic account on running text for the Pahlavi hypothesis
statement: I manually counted the 18 example columns in Appendix B, p. 15, of Herrmann's 2017 v2 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1709.01634v2), using the table's Vt row for Voynich transcription choices and Pt for proposed Pahlavi forms. Three Pt entries explicitly print two alternatives separated by a slash (blood, separation or distribute, and name or cause); one more slash separates two candidates glossed as two or evil, for four total. Two other Pt entries are marked with question marks and one has bracketed completion. Three Vt entries mark ignored characters with parentheses. Two of those combine material across a line break for versions of Spandarmad. One separate Vt entry prints two transcriptions (Mdoy/Adwg). These are counts of printed choices, with any unprinted alternatives outside the audit. The notes report that leading o is retained in otr but discarded after the line break in Spandarmad, and propose a contraction to account for an ignored a. I found no fixed rule in Tables 1–2 or the Appendix B notes that selects those treatments from visible glyph context before a proposed word is chosen, and no connected translation for the 18 columns is provided. The author's running-text example establishes the need for explicit selection rules and independent testing before it can support a complete phonemic account.
check: Have a Pahlavi specialist specify, before testing, the segmentation and context rules for o, ignored marks, ligatures, multi-glyph outputs, possible insertions and across-line joining. Freeze the rules and retain unresolved outputs as alternatives. Require two independent reviewers to apply them to previously unused contiguous public passages with illustrations masked and to length-matched shuffled controls. Report agreement on glyph alignments, recurring stems and inflection, candidate counts before narrowing, and independently produced connected translations.
